_source: Which feed belongs to which site was read off each sibling repository's own feed.xml -- the <atom:link rel="self"> each generator writes -- rather than guessed from the domain. Two of them publish more than one feed, so the choice of WHICH feed a wire carries is a curation decision and it is recorded here per wire, named on the page, and linked. Nothing on this board was typed from memory.
_order: The running order is stimpunks.org's own, off its published feeds page: the blog first, then Star Stuff, Queering.Earth, Cavendish Space, Penguin Pebbling, The Why Sheet Press, this street, and the Map of Monotropic Experiences. That page is the one place our sites are collected by somebody deciding, and re-sorting it here -- alphabetically, or by which wire had something newest -- would be this room quietly overruling a decision made somewhere else. The Jungle Room keeps its cams in the events page's own groups for the same reason.
_itself: THIS STREET IS ON ITS OWN BOARD, on purpose. A board that listed every sibling and left itself off would be claiming to be the station rather than a platform in it. stimpunks.love's changelog feed is read over the network exactly like the rest, which means the board can be wrong about this site too, and is set at the same minute.
_no_body: A row carries a title, a date and where it goes. Never a summary, never an excerpt, never the item's content. A departures board gives you a name and a time; it does not read you the contents of the train. That is the room's argument and it is also what keeps this page from republishing everybody else's writing onto one surface. make-arrivals.py refuses a row with a summary field on it, because the friendly edit -- the rows look bare, paste the excerpts back in -- is a real one and it will arrive.
_no_ranking: No wire is ranked and no site's activity is totalled. There is no busiest, no quietest, no this-week count and nothing that says which of our sites has been getting on with it. A board that showed that would turn publishing into a race between our own people, most of whom are Disabled and several of whom are one person -- the pebbling cabinet's refusal of a tally, arriving between sites rather than inside a game.
_snapshot: The board is set when the site is built and not when somebody looks at it. None of these hosts sends an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so a browser cannot read these feeds from the page, and the ways round that are a proxy we do not run or a third-party reader we would be handing our visitors to. So every wire records the minute it was read, the hall says when the board was set, and every feed is linked so the live thing is one press away. The board is not the railway.

_prose: A wire may carry a `prose` name as well as its nameboard one, for the sentences make-arrivals.py writes. The Map of Monotropic Experiences takes an article in a sentence and does not take one on a sign, and a generated sentence that reads like a generated sentence is the thing generating it was supposed to avoid.
